From my understanding, maths exam rubrics (even at the school level) are quite detailed with how many marks for each answer and even the criteria for partial marks for partially correct answers and there is a high level of marking consistency.

For language subjects, the level of detail in the rubric would be dependent on the type of questions used. Discrete questions with single answers (more used in lower years) would lend themselves to a detailed rubric, but essay type questions (more used in higher years) are harder to evaluate consistently. Therefore you would expect more leeway for marks to vary in language subjects based on knowledge of the identity of the student.
